content:
Summit morning on Point Lenana (4,985 m) starts around 2:00-3:00am below freezing, so the Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi worth paying for is whatever keeps you warm and dry for those hours: broken-in waterproof boots, a base layer, fleece and insulated jacket under a shell, two pairs of gloves, a warm hat and a bright headlamp.

Most climbers get the big items roughly right and then come unstuck on details: boots bought the week before, one pair of thin gloves, a headlamp whose batteries die in the cold. Below we work backwards from summit night to show which Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi to buy and what to look for on the rail.

Quick Facts

  • Trekking summit: Point Lenana, 4,985 m; Batian (5,199 m) and Nelion (5,188 m) are technical climbs
  • Coldest hours: the pre-dawn summit push, usually below freezing and colder in wind
  • Gates from Nairobi: Naro Moru about 188 km, Sirimon about 200 km, Chogoria about 210 km
  • Sleeping bag: three- or four-season, comfort rating of about -5°C or lower
  • Drier months: January-February and July-September; long rains roughly March-May, short rains roughly October-December
  • Where to shop: Mountain Mall, 3rd Floor, Shop D39, Thika Road, or online with M-Pesa or cash on delivery

What Mt Kenya Gear in Nairobi Do You Actually Need to Buy?

Most climbers only need to buy personal clothing and footwear: boots, socks, base layers, a fleece, an insulated jacket, a waterproof shell and rain pants, gloves, a warm hat, a headlamp and a daypack. Tents, cooking kit and meals normally come with an organised climb.

Ask your climbing operator for its written kit list and what it includes or hires out. Whatever is left on the personal side is the Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi you need to buy or borrow, and that is where the budget should go. Our Mt Kenya packing list covers every item day by day.

Which pieces should you buy first?

Buy boots first, because they need two to four weeks of walking before they are safe on a five-day climb. The warm jacket and shell come next, and small items last.

  1. Hiking boots, worn on two or three day hikes around Nairobi.
  2. Insulated jacket, down or synthetic, for summit night.
  3. Waterproof shell jacket and rain pants.
  4. Base layers and a fleece mid layer.
  5. Liner gloves plus an insulated pair, a beanie or balaclava, and a sun hat.
  6. Headlamp with spare power, two water bottles and a 25-35 litre daypack.

How Cold Does Mt Kenya Get, Zone by Zone?

Mt Kenya runs from humid forest to freezing alpine rock in three or four days. Nights at high camps such as Shipton's (around 4,200 m) drop below freezing, while midday sun at the same altitude can burn exposed skin.

That spread is why a single heavy coat is the wrong buy. Treat Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi as a system: layers let you strip down in the forest and wear everything at once on the summit push; our post on layering for cold weather hikes explains how they work together.

What to Look for When Buying Mt Kenya Gear in Nairobi

Judge every item by warmth for its weight, real waterproofing, fit over your other layers and sound zips and seams.

Boots and socks for Mt Kenya

Waterproof, ankle-height boots with a deep-lugged sole handle all three standard routes: forest mud, wet moorland tussock and loose scree on the final climb. Fit them with a thick sock and leave a thumb's width in front of your toes for the descent.

The Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid pairs a waterproof membrane with a supportive mid cut. When you shop for Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi, add three or four pairs of merino wool hiking socks, which stay warm when damp.

Jackets and layers

Plan on three upper layers under a shell: a wicking base layer, a fleece and an insulated jacket. Each must fit over the one beneath without pulling at the shoulders.

Down gives the most warmth for its weight but loses loft when soaked, so carry it in a dry bag; synthetic fill copes better with damp tents. Our guide to down jackets in Nairobi compares fill power. The shell is the piece of Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi most worth buying from a proper outdoor brand, so browse our rain jackets for taped seams, a hood that fits over a beanie and a storm flap over the zip.

Gloves, hats and balaclavas

Two glove layers work better than one thick pair. Thin liners let you open zips and snack wrappers without baring skin, while an insulated waterproof pair goes on for the summit push.

Outers such as these Thinsulate waterproof hiking gloves suit Mt Kenya's wet cold. Gloves are also the cheapest Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi to double up on. Add a beanie that covers your ears, a sun hat, and a fleece-lined balaclava for the wind above Austrian Hut.

Headlamp, poles and gaiters

Summit night means three or more hours of walking in the dark, so choose a headlamp of around 200 lumens or more.

A waterproof rechargeable headlamp fits that job if you carry a small power bank. Waterproof leg gaiters keep bog water and scree out of your boots, and foldable trekking poles spare your knees on the long descent. These three items round off your Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi without costing much.

Is Thrifted Mt Kenya Gear in Nairobi Worth Buying?

Thrifted mountain kit is often the best value, because good boots, shells and down jackets are built to last many seasons.

Our shop sells quality thrifted gear plus some new items, which puts a full set of Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi within reach of more climbers. Spend on what protects you on summit night and save on camp clothes. Before paying for any second-hand piece, look it over yourself using the table below; our post on second hand hiking boots in Nairobi goes deeper on soles.

ItemWhat to look forWalk away if

Waterproof shellSeam tape intact, hood toggles workThe inner membrane is flaking or sticky
Hiking bootsDeep tread, sole firmly bondedThe sole is lifting or lugs are worn flat
GlovesEven insulation, cuffs that cinchThe lining is torn at the fingertips
Sleeping bagLoft springs back, zip runs freelyIt stays flat or smells damp

Pro Tips Before the Gate

  • Dress rehearsal: wear every layer at once on a cold morning walk
  • Dry bags: pack the sleeping bag and insulated jacket in waterproof bags inside the porter bag
  • Warm batteries: keep headlamp batteries and your phone in an inside chest pocket
  • Camp shoes: light trainers or sandals let boots and feet dry out at camp

How Should You Test Mt Kenya Gear in Nairobi Before the Climb?

Test your kit on at least two real hikes: one long, steep day to break in boots and one cold, wet day to prove your layers and waterproofs. Problems found near Nairobi are cheap to fix; at 4,000 m they can end the climb.

The crater rim in our Mt Longonot hike guide gives a hard day on loose volcanic ash, like summit scree in miniature. For cold and wet, an early start on Elephant Hill in the Aberdares shows whether your new Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi keeps water out. What gear mistakes do first-time Mt Kenya climbers make?

First-timers most often bring brand-new boots, rely on one pair of gloves, pack a cotton hoodie as the warm layer, or bury the down jacket in the porter bag. All four are easy to put right while you shop for Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi, and the last one costs nothing: keep a warm layer and the shell in your daypack.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi cost?

Kit for Mt Kenya costs much less when you buy quality thrifted pieces and skip anything your operator already supplies. Boots and the insulated jacket take the biggest share of the budget. Check current prices for Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi on our product pages, then put most of your money into what keeps you warm on summit night.

Do I need special boots for Point Lenana?

Point Lenana does not need mountaineering boots. Waterproof, ankle-supporting hiking boots with a deep-lugged sole are enough on the Sirimon, Naro Moru and Chogoria routes, as long as they are broken in and fit a thick wool sock. Technical climbs on Batian or Nelion need specialist footwear.

Can I climb Mt Kenya in a normal jacket?

A normal city jacket is not enough for Mt Kenya, because the summit push starts in the small hours below freezing and often in wind. Climbers need an insulated down or synthetic jacket over a base layer and fleece, plus a waterproof shell on top. Whatever Mt Kenya gear in Nairobi you skip, do not skip the shell.

What sleeping bag rating do you need for Mt Kenya?

Mt Kenya climbers should bring a three- or four-season sleeping bag with a comfort rating of about -5°C or lower, since nights at Shipton's and Mackinder's camps drop below freezing. Ask your operator first whether one is provided; our sleeping bags in Nairobi post explains the ratings.

Final Thoughts

Plan backwards from the coldest three hours of the climb. If your boots are broken in, your layers stack under a working shell and your hands, head and headlamp are covered twice over, the rest of the kit list is easy.
